'''Jorge Mateu''' is a Spanish [[mathematician]], author, and academic. He is a professor of [[statistics]] within the Department of Mathematics at [[Jaume I University|University Jaume I of Castellon]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uji.es/departaments/com/base/estructura/personal/?p_profesor=65406|title=Jorge Mateu Mahiques - Universitat Jaume I}}</ref> and director of the Unit Eurocop for Data Science in criminal activities in the same department.<ref name=tgf/>

Mateu's research is centered on [[data science]], [[geostatistics]], and [[stochastic processes]], with a particular emphasis on [[Spatiotemporal pattern|spatio-temporal]] [[point process]]es.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://community.wolfram.com/web/mateu|title=Jorge Mateu: Member Profile—Wolfram Community|website=community.wolfram.com}}</ref> He led the 'Mathematical-statistical modelling of [[Spacetime|space-time]] data and [[data mining]]' group at Universitat Jaume I to develop spatio-temporal statistical techniques used for [[Modeling and simulation|modelling]] across fields of [[Public security|public safety]], [[Environmental resource management|environmental management]], and [[criminology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ruvid.org/ri-world/uji-research-team-offers-modeling-techniques-that-allow-planning-in-areas-such-as-pollution-epidemiology-or-safety/|title=UJI research team offers modeling techniques that allow planning in areas such as pollution, epidemiology or safety}}</ref> He is co-editor of books, including ''Spatial Statistics Through Applications'' (2002), ''Case Studies in Spatial Point Process Modeling'' (2005), ''Spatio-temporal Design''. ''Advances in Efficient Data Acquisition'' (2012), ''Spatial and Spatio-Temporal Geostatistical Modeling and Kriging'' (2015), or ''Geostatistical Functional Data Analysis'' (2021). He has also received the Social Council Award from UJI and has been noted as a World Class Professor by an [[Ministry of Education and Culture (Indonesia)|Indonesian ministry]].<ref name=ind>{{cite web|url=https://www.its.ac.id/international/2022/09/18/international-seminar-on-world-class-professor-program/|title=International Seminar on World Class Professor Program}}</ref>

Mateu is a Fellow of the [[Royal Statistical Society]] and [[Wessex Institute of Technology|Wessex Institute]] in [[Great Britain]] and a member of The [[International Statistical Institute]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2022/02/01/2022-editors/|title=Meet the ASA's 2022 Incoming Editors &#124; Amstat News|date=February 1, 2022}}</ref> and the [[Bernoulli Society for Mathematical Statistics and Probability]]. He served as a guest editor for special issues in the ''[[Journal of Geophysical Research]]'', and ''Environmetrics'', as the editor-in-chief for the ''[[Journal of Agricultural, Biological, and Environmental Statistics]]''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.springer.com/journal/13253|title=Journal of Agricultural, Biological and Environmental Statistics|website=Springer}}</ref> as well as an associate editor for ''Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.springer.com/journal/477/editors|title=Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment|website=Springer}}</ref> ''[[Spatial Statistics]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/spatial-statistics/editorial-board/journals.elsevier.com/spatial-statistics/editorial-board/jorge-mateu|title=Jorge Mateu - Editorial Board - Spatial Statistics - Journal - Elsevier|website=www.journals.elsevier.com}}</ref> ''Environmetrics'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/1099095x/homepage/editorialboard.html|title=Environmetrics}}</ref> and ''International Statistical Review''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/17515823/homepage/editorialboard.html|title=International Statistical Review}}</ref>

==Education==
Mateu earned his undergraduate degree in [[mathematics]] and [[statistics]] from the [[University of Valencia]] in 1987, followed by a master's degree in 1995. He graduated with a Ph.D. from the Department of Mathematics at University of Valencia (UV) in 1998.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.springer.com/journal/13253/updates/20032466|title=Journal of Agricultural, Biological and Environmental Statistics|website=Springer}}</ref>

==Career==
Mateu began his academic career as an [[assistant professor]] of statistics in the Department of Mathematics at Jaume I University in 1992<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.its.ac.id/international/experiencing-its/international-lecturer/adjunct-professor/|title=ITS Adjunct Professors}}</ref> where he served as an associate professor from 2000 to 2007. In 2007, he assumed the position of Full Professor of Statistics at UJI.<ref name="ieeexplore.ieee.org">{{Cite journal|doi=10.1109/ACCESS.2020.3036715 |s2cid=227232920 |title=Spatio-Temporal Prediction of Baltimore Crime Events Using CLSTM Neural Networks |date=2020 |last1=Esquivel |first1=Nicolas |last2=Nicolis |first2=Orietta |last3=Peralta |first3=Billy |last4=Mateu |first4=Jorge |journal=IEEE Access |volume=8 |pages=209101–209112 |bibcode=2020IEEEA...8t9101E |doi-access=free |hdl=10234/192286 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

In 2011, he held the position of secretary for the International Environmetrics Society's board of directors<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.environmetrics.org/Newsletters/Public/2011-06.pdf|title=Newsletter Volume 17, No. 1, June 2011}}</ref> and became a co-director of the [[Erasmus Mundus]] Master in Geospatial Technologies.<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://shum.cc.huji.ac.il/~oman/glim/copula.article.pdf|doi=10.1007/s10651-017-0379-x |title=Modelling count data based on weakly dependent spatial covariates using a copula approach: Application to rat sightings |date=2017 |last1=Gräler |first1=Benedikt |last2=Ayyad |first2=Carlos |last3=Mateu |first3=Jorge |journal=Environmental and Ecological Statistics |volume=24 |issue=3 |pages=433–448 |bibcode=2017EnvES..24..433G |s2cid=254471945 }}</ref> Additionally, he served as President of the [[Editorial board|Board of Editors]] for METMA Workshops<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sew2022.sciencesconf.org/|title=20th Edition of the International Workshop on Spatial Econometrics and Statistics - Sciencesconf.org|website=sew2022.sciencesconf.org}}</ref> Since 2014, he has been serving as the director of the Unit Eurocop: Statistical Modeling of Crime Data at Jaume I University.<ref name=tgf>{{cite web|url=https://eprints.lancs.ac.uk/id/eprint/139589/2/StatScience_interview_to_PDiggle_Atkinson_Mateu_27Feb2019_Revisedversion_final_form.pdf|title=A Conversation with Peter Diggle}}</ref>

==Research==
Mateu focuses his research on the [[intersection]] of geostatistics, [[Spatial database|spatial data]], stochastic processes, [[computational science]]s, and [[natural science]]s, with a particular emphasis on [[data science]]. He has analysed [[Crime statistics|crime data]] and [[public health]] projects by employing a combination of statistical and [[Machine learning|machine-learning]] methods.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amstat.org/publications/q-and-as/meet-the-asa-s-2022-incoming-editors|title=Meet the ASA's 2022 Incoming Editors|website=Default}}</ref> He served as a joint [[principal investigator]] for GEO-C.<ref>{{Cite thesis|url=https://run.unl.pt/handle/10362/11547?locale=en|title=Using GIS to map the spatial and temporal occurrence of cholera epidemic in Camaroon|first=Ayuk Sally|last=Agbor|date=February 28, 2014|type=Master's Thesis |hdl=10362/11547}}</ref> He was worked on the projects (a) Statistical analysis of complex dependencies in space-time stochastic processes. Networks, functional marks and SPDE-based intensities. Ministry of Science and bInnovation (PID2022-141555OB-I00), 2023-2026, and (b) Spatio-temporal stochastic processes over networks and trajectories. Parametric models and functional marks. Generalitat Valenciana (CIAICO/2022/191), 2023-2025.

===Data science and stochastic processes===
Mateu's research on data science has included a range of topics such as filament delineation, [[model selection]], and stochastic processes. In his research on the automatic delineation of filaments obtained from redshift catalogs, he applied a marked point process, to gain insights into the cosmic filament structure.<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361:20042409 | doi=10.1051/0004-6361:20042409 | title=Detection of cosmic filaments using the Candy model | date=2005 | last1=Stoica | first1=R. S. | last2=Martínez | first2=V. J. | last3=Mateu | first3=J. | last4=Saar | first4=E. | journal=Astronomy & Astrophysics | volume=434 | issue=2 | pages=423–432 | arxiv=astro-ph/0405370 | bibcode=2005A&A...434..423S | s2cid=3078877 }}</ref> Together with a number of coauthors, he extended Gneiting's work to develop new spatio-temporal covariance models, resulting in novel classes of stationary nonseparable functions.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s00477-006-0048-3|title=Nonseparable stationary anisotropic space–time covariance functions|first1=E.|last1=Porcu|first2=P.|last2=Gregori|first3=J.|last3=Mateu|date=December 1, 2006|journal=Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment|volume=21|issue=2|pages=113–122|via=Springer Link|doi=10.1007/s00477-006-0048-3|bibcode=2006SERRA..21..113P |s2cid=121599229 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> In addition, his research of space-time [[covariance function]] estimation introduced two methods based on the concept of composite likelihood which were designed to strike a balance between computational complexity and statistical efficiency.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/01621459.2011.646928|title=Estimating Space and Space-Time Covariance Functions for Large Data Sets: A Weighted Composite Likelihood Approach|first1=Moreno|last1=Bevilacqua|first2=Carlo|last2=Gaetan|first3=Jorge|last3=Mateu|first4=Emilio|last4=Porcu|date=March 14, 2012|journal=Journal of the American Statistical Association|volume=107|issue=497|pages=268–280|via=CrossRef|doi=10.1080/01621459.2011.646928|hdl=10234/68502 |s2cid=121529248 |hdl-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Furthermore, while addressing the challenge of model selection, he discussed the limitations of traditional models like [[Bayesian information criterion|Bayesian Information Criterion]] and proposed a practical extension aimed at handling model selection issues effectively.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1111/rssb.12187 | title=A Bayesian Information Criterion for Singular Models | date=2017 | last1=Drton | first1=Mathias | last2=Plummer | first2=Martyn | journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B: Statistical Methodology | volume=79 | issue=2 | pages=323–380 | s2cid=15334628 | doi-access=free | hdl=10.1111/rssb.12187 | hdl-access=free | arxiv=1309.0911 }}</ref> In 2018, during his research on the use of administrative data, he identified challenges related to statistical analyses and discussed the need for a critical approach to ensure the validity and accuracy of results.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1111/rssa.12315 | title=Statistical Challenges of Administrative and Transaction Data | date=2018 | last1=Hand | first1=David J. | journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A: Statistics in Society | volume=181 | issue=3 | pages=555–605 | s2cid=126301517 | doi-access=free | hdl=10044/1/61527 | hdl-access=free }}</ref>

===Spatial data and environmental management===
Mateu has conducted studies on the spatial and spatio-temporal point processes. He conducted research to analyse spatial point patterns across different experimental groups, summarising his findings using the K-function in a non-parametric approach to emphasise the strengths and limitations of spatial data.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/advances-in-applied-probability/article/abs/comparison-between-parametric-and-nonparametric-approaches-to-the-analysis-of-replicated-spatial-point-patterns/71AAE5CFE60B44F0988DBE0775DA1D40|title=A comparison between parametric and non-parametric approaches to the analysis of replicated spatial point patterns|first1=Peter J.|last1=Diggle|first2=Jorge|last2=Mateu|first3=Helen E.|last3=Clough|date=June 14, 2000|journal=Advances in Applied Probability|volume=32|issue=2|pages=331–343|via=Cambridge University Press|doi=10.1239/aap/1013540166|s2cid=120635354 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> His work on Functional Data Analysis demonstrated its connection with three traditional types of spatial data structures and provided examples to illustrate the integration of geostatistical data, and areal data.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/env.1003|title=Statistics for spatial functional data: some recent contributions|first1=P.|last1=Delicado|first2=R.|last2=Giraldo|first3=C.|last3=Comas|first4=J.|last4=Mateu|date=May 14, 2010|journal=Environmetrics|volume=21|issue=3–4|pages=224–239|via=CrossRef|doi=10.1002/env.1003|bibcode=2010Envir..21..224D |s2cid=120192912 |url-access=subscription|hdl=2117/8739|hdl-access=free}}</ref> He also introduced a methodological framework based on geostatistics that applied to agricultural planning and environmental restoration.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s00254-003-0894-y|title=Spatial dynamics of soil salinity under arid and semi-arid conditions: geological and environmental implications|first1=M. M.|last1=Jordán|first2=J.|last2=Navarro-Pedreño|first3=E.|last3=García-Sánchez|first4=J.|last4=Mateu|first5=P.|last5=Juan|date=February 1, 2004|journal=Environmental Geology|volume=45|issue=4|pages=448–456|via=Springer Link|doi=10.1007/s00254-003-0894-y|s2cid=53125885 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> In collaboration with other colleagues, he analysed real-world soil penetration and presented an approach for predicting spatial patterns in functional data which enabled the estimation of values at unobserved locations.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s10651-010-0143-y|title=Ordinary kriging for function-valued spatial data|first1=R.|last1=Giraldo|first2=P.|last2=Delicado|first3=J.|last3=Mateu|date=September 1, 2011|journal=Environmental and Ecological Statistics|volume=18|issue=3|pages=411–426|via=Springer Link|doi=10.1007/s10651-010-0143-y|bibcode=2011EnvES..18..411G |s2cid=40403028 |url-access=subscription|hdl=2117/9246|hdl-access=free}}</ref>

===Crime data and public health analysis===
Mateu's research on functional environmental data, particularly in modelling air pollutant concentrations, emphasised the importance of cross-validation for parameter selection and provided insights into adapting kriging techniques.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s00477-013-0806-y|title=Kriging with external drift for functional data for air quality monitoring|first1=Rosaria|last1=Ignaccolo|first2=Jorge|last2=Mateu|first3=Ramon|last3=Giraldo|date=July 1, 2014|journal=Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment|volume=28|issue=5|pages=1171–1186|via=Springer Link|doi=10.1007/s00477-013-0806-y|bibcode=2014SERRA..28.1171I |s2cid=53375199 |hdl=2318/137791|hdl-access=free}}</ref> In 2003, he introduced a spatiotemporal Hawkes-type point process model for analysing violence by incorporating daily and weekly periodic patterns in crime occurrences to shed light on the interplay of temporal trends in crime.<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://doi.org/10.1111/rssa.12429 | doi=10.1111/rssa.12429 | title=A Semiparametric Spatiotemporal Hawkes-Type Point Process Model with Periodic Background for Crime Data | date=2019 | last1=Zhuang | first1=Jiancang | last2=Mateu | first2=Jorge | journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A: Statistics in Society | volume=182 | issue=3 | pages=919–942 | s2cid=125818982 | url-access=subscription }}</ref> Expanding on this research, he introduced a deep learning approach in temporal correlations of historical data resulting in the enhancement of police resources, surveillance, crime event predictions, and prevention strategies.<ref name="ieeexplore.ieee.org"/>
